Chords between nodes

Source: R/geom-chord.R
geom_chord.Rd

A chord leaves each of its two endpoint arcs at the slot the layout reserved for it, so links read as a banded ring rather than a star burst from node centres. Two shapes are available: type = "ribbon" fills the area between the two curves of a link, type = "line" draws a single curve from one slot to the other.

Usage

geom_chord(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  type = c("ribbon", "line"),
  curvature = "auto",
  ncp = 40,
  alpha = NULL,
  linewidth = NULL,
  arrow = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, show.legend, inherit.aes, na.rm, ...

Standard ggplot2::layer() arguments.

from, to

Unquoted column names of the link endpoints. Required when data is supplied; otherwise the layout's link table is used as is.

type

"ribbon" (filled area) or "line" (single curve).

curvature

"auto" derives the bulge from how far apart the two slots are – opposite slots reach the centre. A number overrides it: 1 always bulges to the centre.

ncp

Number of points sampled along each curve.

alpha, linewidth

Line width / ribbon opacity defaults.

arrow

Optional arrow specification for type = "line".

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

The default data is the layout's link table, in which the coordinates are already computed. To style a subset of the links, pass data plus the two endpoint columns – either as arguments (from = , to = ) or through the mapping (aes(from = , to = )).

Geometry

For a slot pair [a0, a1] and [b0, b1], let d be the shortest signed angular distance between the two facing slot edges. The control point radius is k = 1 - 4|d| / (3pi), which is 1 for adjacent slots (the curve stays on the ring) and -1/3 for opposite slots (the curve passes through the centre). The control points share the endpoints' angles, so every chord leaves the ring radially.

Examples

m <- cor(mtcars)
ggcircos(m, order = "hclust") +
    geom_chord(aes(fill = r)) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = 0)
